games.note: P0 ramps, casts Lathiel (turn ~5), casts a Grizzly Bears; P1 casts one Grizzly Bears. Turn 17: P0 attacks P1's player with Lathiel alone (lifelink) -> P0 life 20->22 (gained 2). P1 declares no blockers. End step: Lathiel trigger fires (TriggerTargetSelection, source_id 24, description matches oracle text). Slot 0: driver targets own bear (oid 13) - accepted. Slot 1: candidates contain ONLY P1's bear (oid 102); own bear excluded (unique:true). Driver submits empty selection (decline/up-to path) - accepted. Post: own bear has 2 P1P1 counters, P1 bear 0.

notes: Parse layer (pinned v0.80.0 card-data.json, parse_evidence.json): Lathiel's end-step trigger is supported but encodes multi_target={min:0, max:Ref(LifeGainedThisTurn)} - the target-count cap is tied to life gained, conflating the counter budget with oracle's independently variable 'any number' of targets.

Runtime manifestation (target_prompt.json): the engine presents the trigger as N=life-gained sequential target slots (here 2 slots), each a sequence schema {min:0, max:1, unique:true, confirm:explicit}. Slot 1's candidates EXCLUDE the creature chosen in slot 0 - the same creature cannot be selected twice.

With a single own creature on board, the engine's slot-1 offer was exactly one candidate: the OPPONENT's Grizzly Bears (oid 102). The only way to avoid targeting it was the empty-selection decline path (min:0). This is the reported experience: the ability plays as 'distribute among THAT MANY distinct creatures', steering the controller toward opponent creatures.

Decline-path quirk, recorded honestly: after declining slot 1, the post state shows the own bear (oid 13) with 2 P1P1 counters and the opponent bear with 0 - the engine distributed both counters onto the single chosen target rather than dropping the declined counter. The defect is in the target-selection model (distinct slots, re-selection forbidden), not in the final tally of this particular line.

A6 passed: an up-to decline path exists (empty selection accepted), so the controller is not literally forced onto the opponent's creature - but stacking counters is only expressible via decline, never by selecting the same creature twice.
